title: Blue Jays DFA offseason addition Jesús Sánchez, call up minor-league veteran
content:
The Toronto Blue Jays have designated outfielder Jesús Sánchez for assignment, parting ways with an offseason trade addition who failed to find his footing with them. Outfielder Rudy Martin Jr. was promoted to make his MLB debut 12 years after he was selected in the 25th round of the 2014 MLB Draft.

Sánchez, who came to Toronto from the Houston Astros in exchange for Joey Loperfido during spring training, was expected to provide some of the power lost when Anthony Santander underwent shoulder surgery in the spring. The former Miami Marlins and Astros outfielder had 73 homers across six big-league seasons before the trade, consistently performing against right-handed pitching.

Though Sánchez hit eight home runs for Toronto and posted a .734 OPS that ranks above league average, his defensive play made it increasingly difficult to find him playing time. He lost two fly balls in the roof at Tropicana Field in Toronto’s 7-6 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in August and dropped another in the Jays’ 6-1 loss at the Kansas City Royals last week. The 28-year-old’s outs above average (minus-8) rank among the worst outfielders in baseball this year.

Sánchez had a clear role on a Jays team starved for power this year. With Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s struggles, George Springer’s up-and-down, injury-filled campaign and Addison Barger’s injury, the Jays could stomach some below-average defence if Sánchez provided thump. With just one homer and a .656 OPS in the second half, though, Sánchez’s offensive potential hasn’t flashed enough recently to stick on a Jays team still hoping for the playoffs.

With Myles Straw, Brett Bateman and Nathan Lukes regularly playing in the outfield and Springer at designated hitter, there wasn’t much room for a struggling Sánchez. Martin, Josh Smith, Charles McAdoo and potentially soon Santander could also contribute to the outfield mix. Santander began a rehab assignment with Triple-A Buffalo on Wednesday.

Martin, a 30-year-old base-stealing threat, has played nine minor-league seasons, plus brief stints in the Mexican League and independent ball. The Jays picked him up off waivers from the Orioles earlier this year, and he owns an .815 OPS across 91 minor-league games this season. He also has 45 stolen bases on 53 attempts this year, adding some speed to Toronto’s bench.
